intro.text: A machine the visiting scholars in Gongsha Town mention while struggling with their own stone-stacking device. Their leader says the father machine never gave them such trouble.

A great machine first set running 1,763 years ago, during the Festival of Reveals. It was meant to feed on the spirits' power, but it consumed the people of Torio instead. Only the yoki-hijo withstood it.
A machine made by Torio City scholars to pile stones, draw hijo to it and turn their power into hion. Its activation gave rise to the shroud and made nightmares of most of Torio's people.

description.text: Torio City's Institute of Mechanical Solutions designed it to lure hijo with stone stacks, then use their power to produce hion and send it out.
The father machine towers thirty feet high over the exhibit hall that houses it, piling up and knocking down stones with hundreds of legs.

items.text: The scholars set it running 1,763 years ago, during the Festival of Reveals. It consumed the people of Torio rather than drawing on the spirits, and the yoki-hijo, the only ones to resist, were held captive from then on.

University scholars in Torio City first built a prototype that stacked simple piles of rock, drawing spirits slowly but steadily and siphoning off part of their souls to keep running. This led to the father machine, far larger and able to make hion lines.

Gyundok and his scholars switched it on at the Festival of Reveals, when Yumi was nineteen. A gap in its instructions led it to take human souls before turning to the hijo, and it consumed nearly everyone in Torio except the nomads on the kingdom's fringes. The waste became the shroud. After that it ran on the hijo and grew hion stubs that burst out of the ground in nearby villages.
The yoki-hijo's souls were too strong for it to destroy, so it shut them away in fake towns and changed their memories each day so they never knew they were prisoners.

Things stayed this way for over 1,700 years. Then a handful of hijo slipped free and made contact with Futinoro's people. To keep Nagadan from learning the truth, the machine sent a small army of stable nightmares to wipe out the city, an event the scholars called the Incident.

Some decades after that, another spirit broke free and reached Yumi. By Connecting her to Nikaro, it stopped the machine from changing her memories. The machine first let her move on to a new town each day, but when she stayed in Gongsha Town it sent Gyundok's scholars and the prototype to investigate and catch the spirit. They discovered the spirit's work and cut the link between the two.

The machine tried to cover over Yumi's memories, but she broke through and remembered Painter. In Torio City its shield kept her back, so she raised towering stone stacks that pulled the hijo away from it. It worked faster and wilder but could not keep up, ground to a stop, and, with few of its first parts left, crumbled away along with the shroud and the nightmares.

Its orders were to draw power from spirits, which turned out to include souls, and to protect itself. What it takes from the hijo creates and runs the hion lines, which it grows up out of the ground across the countryside.

Under threat it stacks faster but more carelessly. It guards itself with a clear barrier that people cannot cross, rebuilds its parts from smoky power drawn from spirits, and can turn nightmares against its attackers. Its store of power has given it a kind of awareness.

Other devices can be plugged into the scholars' machine: a finder whose needle swings toward spirits close by, a trap for catching them, and one that cuts Connections, which is used to separate Yumi and Nikaro.

A smaller prototype was built first to test the father machine's workings. Built of metal and about as big as a chest of drawers, it looks like a spider with its dozens of rod-shaped arms, and it hums softly as it stacks stones and clears away fallen ones.

The prototype needs a power source, such as the Investiture of a spirit or a nightmare, and a plate behind a side panel lets someone prime it. Spirits it summons can be bound with images but work less well than those bound by a yoki-hijo, since the machine keeps back part of each spirit's soul to keep running.
The scholars who come to Gongsha Town to look into Yumi bring this prototype with them.
